cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven strip cloth of narrow cotton bands stitched together, with indigo and white checkerboard ground and supplementary-weft geometric motifs — a classic West African Mande-tradition strip-weave, consistent with Dyula (a Mande-speaking trading/weaving people) production.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Cloth; composed of eight narrow cotton strips of (apparently) imported European industrial cotton, hand-woven and hand-sewn along the the selvedges. The warp is of white cotton, and the ground weft alternates white and dark blue cotton, and uses supplementary weft threads in cream, yellow, red and light blue. These form small areas of pattern that are positioned in the centre of each dark blue square. The warps are aligned to form a chequerboard pattern across the cloth. At each end is a band of dark blue cotton, and the warp ends have been left as a fringe.
